metadata.title: Double progenitor origin of the S-star cluster

evidence.quote: V24 identify a single previously known HVS, S5-HVS1 (Koposov et al. 2020): a 1700 km s<sup>−1</sup> star at about 9 kpc from us that originates in the GC, where it was ejected about 4.8 Myr ago.
S5-HVS1 came from the CWD and shares the same age.
HVSs can travel at ≳ 10<sup>3</sup> km s<sup>−1</sup>, making them unbound to the Galactic potential (Hills 1988; Bromley et al. 2006; Rossi et al. 2014).

V24 identify a single previously known HVS, S5-HVS1 (Koposov et al. 2020): a 1700 km s<sup>−1</sup> star at about 9 kpc from us that originates in the GC, where it was ejected about 4.8 Myr ago. This is the only star unambiguously linked to a GC ejection and provides strong indirect evidence of the Hills mechanism.

In this scenario, S5-HVS1 is about 150 times more likely to have been ejected from the young progenitor population; this, combined with the age estimate for S5-HVS1 of less than 10<sup>8</sup> yr (Koposov et al. 2020) and the alignment of the CWD plane with that of its progenitor binary, leads us to argue that S5-HVS1 came from the CWD and shares the same age.

values.condition: Heliocentric distance of S5-HVS1, quoted as about 9 kpc from us.

values.condition: Speed quoted for S5-HVS1; the paper describes it as a 1700 km/s star without explicitly separating line-of-sight and total Galactic rest-frame speed.

evidence.quote: V24 identify a single previously known HVS, S5-HVS1 (Koposov et al. 2020): a 1700 km s−1 star at about 9 kpc from us that originates in the GC, where it was ejected about 4.8 Myr ago.

notes: S5-HVS1 is a previously known HVS (T:p5-b2) and is retained as the paper's sole observed HVS; the paper argues it came from the CWD (T:p7-b2). The paper's 'S5' (T:p2-b8) is a different S-star, not an alias, and is not grouped here. S111 (T:p2-b8) is omitted by the authors for a hyperbolic orbital solution but is not explicitly identified as Galactic unbound; no other individual unbound candidate is named, and other HVS results concern simulated populations.

S5-HVS1: S5-HVS1 is discussed only briefly in T:p5-b2. The paper reports no equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motion, or bound/unbound probability for it. The distance is explicitly approximate (“about 9 kpc”). The 1700 km/s is a speed; because the paper does not specify whether this is the heliocentric line-of-sight velocity or the total Galactic rest-frame speed, I recorded it as the total speed and flag the ambiguity here. The ejection look-back time of about 4.8 Myr is not one of the requested quantities.
